patients.summary: Retired math teacher with long-standing type 2 diabetes, retinopathy, hypertension and untreated hyperlipidemia who joins in 2019. Over six years he has a healed plantar foot ulcer, REM sleep behavior disorder, thoracic stenosis, CLL on acalabrutinib, metastatic prostate cancer to bone on hormonal therapy, a parapneumonic effusion, and in late 2025 probable sporadic CJD, ending on home hospice.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT

64M, retired HS math teacher, joining after his PCP of many years retired. Here alone.

HPI: Type 2 diabetes since roughly 2001. On metformin 1000 twice a day the whole time, never been on insulin or anything else, and he says the last A1c he remembers was 'in the 8s.' Checks sugars maybe twice a week, fasting numbers 150s-170s. No lows. Eye doctor yearly, told he has diabetic retinopathy, laser never needed as far as he knows. BP on lisinopril 20 and HCTZ 12.5, no home cuff. Told years ago his cholesterol was up; never started anything for it.

ROS: negative except as above. No chest pain, no claudication, no foot sores, no numbness he notices.

PMH: T2DM with retinopathy; HTN; hyperlipidemia (no med).
PSH: none.
Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg daily, HCTZ 12.5 mg daily. Bottles reviewed.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: Father - T2DM, prostate cancer. Mother - HTN, high cholesterol. Maternal uncle - CLL.
SH: Married, lives with his wife in Goshen. Taught high school math for 34 years. Never smoked, does not drink. Gardens, walks the road most mornings.

Exam: Vitals as recorded, BP elevated. Well-appearing, pleasant. Fundi not well seen without dilation. Neck supple, no thyromegaly or nodes. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft. Feet: skin intact, mild callus under both first MT heads, monofilament reduced at the toes and soles both sides, DP and PT pulses 2+ bilaterally. No edema.

A/P:
1. Type 2 diabetes with retinopathy - A1c, CMP, urine microalbumin today. Continue metformin. Will revisit once numbers back.
2. HTN - above goal today, first visit, recheck at follow-up. Continue current two drugs.
3. Hyperlipidemia - lipid panel today.
4. Health maintenance - HCV and HIV screening today. Records request to prior office for colonoscopy and vaccine history. Flu shot next month at a nurse visit.
5. Eye: ask ophthalmology to send this year's exam.

RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Mr. Kerrigan, your labs from Tuesday are back. Kidney function, potassium and blood counts are normal. Hepatitis C and HIV screens negative. Your A1c is above where we want it, and the bad cholesterol (LDL) is mildly high. Urine protein check is normal, which is good news for your kidneys. We'll go over the diabetes numbers together at your December visit.

Exam date: 11/05/2019
Re: Francis Kerrigan, DOB 07/23/1955

events.reason: Diabetes follow-up; right foot odor and drainage

conditions.label: Diabetic foot ulcer of right foot

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Routine DM check, but the main thing today is his right foot.

HPI: 65M. For the past few weeks his wife has noticed a bad smell from his right foot, and he has seen damp spots on his sock, a little clear-yellow fluid now and then. No pain at all, no fever or chills. He mostly wears sandals around the house and admits he is barefoot indoors a fair amount. Didn't think much of it until the smell. Eye surgery in March went fine, reading better.

Meds: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 20, HCTZ 12.5. NKDA.

Exam: T 37.1, BP 142/88, P 84, RR 14.
R foot: shallow ulcer on the plantar surface under the first metatarsal head, surrounded by thick callus, faint pink rim of erythema less than a few mm, no warmth tracking, no fluctuance, base pink and moist, no exposed bone. Mild odor. No lymphangitic streaking.
Sensation diminished in both feet to monofilament. DP/PT pulses palpable bilaterally.

Labs today: WBC 8.4. A1c 8.9.

A/P:
1. Diabetic foot ulcer, R plantar - appears to be healing, no sign of deep infection, afebrile, normal WBC. Foot films today to look at the bone. Urgent podiatry referral for debridement and offloading. No antibiotic for now. Saline dressing daily, keep it covered, and NO bare feet - shoes or closed slippers at all times. Return or call for spreading redness, fever, pain or more drainage.
2. T2DM with retinopathy, A1c 8.9 - continue metformin.
3. HTN - per vitals, continue.

RTC after podiatry.

reports.text: RIGHT FOOT, 3 VIEWS. Indication: plantar ulcer in a diabetic. Soft tissue irregularity at the plantar forefoot beneath the first metatarsal head corresponding to the clinical ulcer. No cortical erosion or periosteal reaction. No soft-tissue gas. No fracture or dislocation. Joint spaces preserved.

documents.title: Foot x-ray
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good news, the x-ray shows no sign that the bone is involved. Podiatry should be calling you this week; let us know if you haven't heard by Friday. Keep the dressing on and keep shoes on in the house.

documents.title: Podiatry consultation
documents.author: podiatry
documents.body:
Podiatry new patient consultation, 05/18/2021
Reason: diabetic plantar ulcer right foot, referred by primary care.

Pt reports drainage and odor for several weeks, painless. Diabetic about 20 years.
Exam: neurovascular - DP and PT palpable bilaterally, capillary refill brisk; protective sensation absent to monofilament at plantar forefoot both feet.
Ulcer: plantar right first metatarsal head, 1.4 x 1.0 x 0.2 cm, granular base, hyperkeratotic rim, no probe to bone, no purulence, minimal periwound erythema.
Right foot radiographs from 05/12 reviewed: no osseous changes.

Procedure: sharp debridement of the surrounding callus and nonviable tissue down to bleeding granulation, tolerated without anesthesia.

Assessment: neuropathic diabetic foot ulcer, right, in the proliferative phase; no infection.
Plan: post-op shoe with felt aperture pad for offloading; saline-moistened gauze daily; no antibiotics indicated. Strict avoidance of barefoot walking. Return in 4-5 weeks.

Allergies: NKDA. Medications: metformin, lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide.

documents.title: Podiatry follow-up
documents.author: podiatry
documents.body: Podiatry follow-up 06/22/2021. Ulcer right sub-first MT head now 0.6 x 0.4 cm, shallow, healthy granulation, no drainage or odor. Callus pared. Continue offloading shoe and daily dressing. Recheck 6-7 weeks.

documents.title: Podiatry follow-up: healed
documents.author: podiatry
documents.body: Seen 08/10/2021. The right plantar ulcer is fully epithelialized. No drainage. Discontinue post-op shoe. Fitted for diabetic depth shoes with custom molded insoles. Routine callus care here every 3 months. Reinforced: shoes or slippers at all times, daily foot inspection. Medications and allergies unchanged (NKDA).

orders.reason: dream enactment behavior with falls from bed

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Here with his wife today. Foot healed - podiatry discharged him from the post-op shoe two weeks ago, now in depth shoes with inserts. Wearing slippers at home.
Wife's concern: for about 3 months he has been thrashing in his sleep - punching, kicking, twice ended up on the floor beside the bed. When she wakes him he describes a dream that matches what he was doing (fending someone off). He is embarrassed about it. No daytime sleepiness, no snoring she's noticed, no trouble falling asleep. No tremor, no change in walking, no memory complaints.

O: Vitals per flowsheet. Alert, conversational, normal speech. No tremor, normal gait and arm swing. R foot: healed, thin callus only. Monofilament still diminished both feet.

A/P:
1. R plantar ulcer - healed, resolved. Podiatry q3 months.
2. Dream enactment with falls - sounds like a REM sleep behavior problem; refer to neurology, they'll likely want a sleep study. Meanwhile pad the floor, move the nightstand away.
3. DM2 - A1c, BMP, lipids, urine microalbumin today.
4. HTN - continue.

RTC 3-4 months.

documents.title: Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Fluzone HD to left arm, Pfizer booster (third dose) to right arm. Over 6 months since his second dose. Waited 15 minutes, no reaction.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth at bedtime

reports.text: Attended overnight in-lab polysomnogram with video. Total sleep time 352 minutes, sleep efficiency 81%. REM sleep present in 4 periods. Persistent elevation of chin and limb EMG tone during REM sleep with phasic limb twitching; video shows arm flailing and kicking during REM. No breathing events of significance; apnea-hypopnea index under 5. Oxygen saturation nadir 91%. No periodic limb movements of significance. No epileptiform activity on the limited EEG montage.
reports.conclusion: REM sleep without atonia with dream enactment, consistent with REM sleep behavior disorder. No significant sleep-disordered breathing.

documents.title: Neurology consultation
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
NEUROLOGY CONSULTATION
Date of service: 11/01/2021
Referring: primary care
Reason: abnormal behaviors in sleep

Dear colleague,

I saw Mr. Kerrigan, a 66-year-old retired teacher with long-standing type 2 diabetes with retinopathy, hypertension and hyperlipidemia, who was treated earlier this year for a right plantar foot ulcer. His wife, who accompanied him, reports about six months of him striking out and kicking while asleep, at times enough to fall from the bed. He is embarrassed by it, and when woken he recalls vivid dreams that fit the movements. Before this began he slept without difficulty.

Medications: metformin, lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg daily. NKDA.
Family history: father diabetes and prostate cancer, mother hypertension and hyperlipidemia, maternal uncle CLL.
Never smoker, no alcohol.

Examination: alert and fully oriented. Speech and language normal. Cranial nerves intact. Tone normal in the waking state; no cogwheeling or rigidity. No rest or postural tremor. Finger and foot tapping brisk, no slowing. Strength full. Gait and turning normal.

Studies: in-lab polysomnography was performed the same night; report enclosed. It demonstrates increased muscle activity during REM sleep with dream enactment captured on video.

Impression: REM sleep behavior disorder.

Recommendations:
1. Bedroom safety: mattress or padding along the bedside, sharp-edged furniture moved, his wife may need to sleep separately on restless nights.
2. Melatonin 3 mg at bedtime.
3. I will see him in about a year, sooner if episodes escalate. We also discussed watching for changes in smell, constipation, movement or thinking, which he should mention to either of us.

Thank you for this referral.

orders.reason: low back pain radiating to thighs with walking

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: back.
Since late November, so about 4 months, aching low back that spreads down into the fronts and sides of both thighs once he has walked several minutes. Has to stop; leaning on a shopping cart helps, sitting down makes it go away. No injury. No bowel/bladder change, no saddle numbness, no fevers, no weight change. Night pain none.

Exam: Vitals as charted. Lumbar paraspinals non-tender. Extension reproduces back pain. Flexion fine. Strength 5/5 legs. Reflexes symmetric. SLR negative both sides. Pedal pulses 2+. Feet: no ulcer.

A/P:
1. Low back pain with leg symptoms brought on by walking, relieved by flexion - sounds like neurogenic claudication; pulses good. Refer to orthopedics spine. Tylenol as needed meanwhile, avoid NSAIDs regularly with the lisinopril/HCTZ.
2. DM2 - A1c today.
3. RBD - on melatonin, stable.

medications.sig: Take 2 tablets by mouth up to three times daily as needed for back pain

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Saw ortho spine 5/2. We never got a note. Per Francis: they examined him, did an MRI the same day, and told him the spinal canal is narrowed in the lower part of the mid-back with thickened ligament. They recommended PT and Tylenol, no surgery talk. Has done 3 PT sessions, exercises daily, says bending forward exercises help. Walking tolerance a little better.

Exam: no change from March. Gait steady.

Plan: Records request to ortho for consult note + MRI report. Rx acetaminophen 500 mg, 2 tabs up to TID PRN (max 3 g/day). Continue PT. Diabetes labs at the next visit (A1c done in March).

reports.text: MRI LUMBAR SPINE WITHOUT CONTRAST. Indication: low back pain radiating to the thighs with walking. Sagittal images include T10 through the sacrum. At T11-T12 the central canal is narrowed by thickening of the ligamentum flavum. Cord signal normal at the levels included; conus ends normally at L1. L1-L2 through L5-S1: disc heights preserved, no significant central canal narrowing, neural foramina patent. Vertebral body heights and marrow signal normal. Paraspinal soft tissues unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Spinal canal narrowing at T11-T12 from ligamentum flavum thickening. No significant lumbar canal narrowing.

documents.title: MRI report received

documents.title: MRI reviewed

documents.title: Neurology follow-up letter
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
NEUROLOGY FOLLOW-UP
Visit date: 10/31/2022

Mr. Kerrigan returns for REM sleep behavior disorder, first evaluated here in November 2021. His wife says the night-time episodes have grown more frequent and forceful: he punches and kicks while asleep and has come out of bed several times, with some minor bumps and bruises. He has no awareness of these events, though he can recall dreams full of action and confrontation.

Current medications: melatonin 3 mg nightly, metformin 1000 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg daily. Allergies: none.
Active issues also include type 2 diabetes with retinopathy, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, thoracic spinal stenosis, and a diabetic foot ulcer of the right foot.

Exam: alert and oriented, attentive, normal recall and conversation. No rigidity, no slowing of repetitive movements, no tremor. Gait normal.

The polysomnogram of November 2021 showed REM sleep without atonia; no repeat study is needed.

Assessment and plan: RBD, clinically worse. Increase melatonin to 6 mg at bedtime. Reviewed bedroom safety again; his wife has started sleeping in the guest room on bad nights. Follow-up in 12 months.

(Letter delayed in transcription; we apologize.)

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: tired, sweats, losing weight.

HPI: 67M. About 7 weeks of feeling worn out by early afternoon, drenching sweats at night a few times a week (changing his T-shirt), eating less, and a full feeling in the belly after small meals. Scale at home down about 10 pounds; today's weight confirms the loss. No fever he's measured, no cough, no bleeding, no change in bowels, no urinary symptoms. Back pain no different. Sleep episodes unchanged on melatonin 6.

Exam: Vitals as charted. Looks tired, a bit pale. Several firm, non-tender, mobile lymph nodes both sides of the neck and in both armpits, 1-2 cm. Abdomen soft, fullness in the LUQ, I think I can feel a spleen tip. No hepatomegaly. Heart regular, lungs clear. No edema. Skin: no petechiae.

CBC with diff and CMP drawn now, asked lab to call.

A/P: Constitutional symptoms with diffuse adenopathy and probable splenomegaly in a man whose uncle had CLL - concerned for a lymphoproliferative disorder. Urgent heme/onc referral placed today; will call him tonight with the CBC.

documents.title: CBC result call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt with CBC: WBC 13.6 with 71% lymphocytes, Hgb 9.4, platelets 156. Explained this fits a blood disorder like the leukemia his uncle had but needs confirmation by hematology. Urgent referral sent; their office will call. Spoke to referral coordinator - appointment 4/27. He and his wife asked good questions. Call sooner for fever, bleeding, worsening breathlessness.

documents.title: Hematology-oncology consultation
documents.author: hematology-oncology
documents.body:
HEMATOLOGY & ONCOLOGY CONSULTATION
Visit: 04/27/2023

Reason for referral: anemia, lymphocytosis and lymphadenopathy.

History: 67-year-old man with type 2 diabetes with retinopathy and a right plantar diabetic foot ulcer, here for two months of fatigue, night sweats and an unintended 10 lb weight loss, along with early fullness and reduced appetite.
Medications: metformin, lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, melatonin. NKDA.
Family: maternal uncle with CLL; father with prostate cancer.

Exam: pallor. Bilateral cervical and axillary adenopathy. Spleen palpable 3 cm below the left costal margin. No hepatomegaly.

Labs today: hemoglobin 9.2 g/dL, MCV 85 fL, WBC 14,000/uL, platelets 150,000/uL, LDH elevated. Peripheral smear reviewed personally: mature-appearing small lymphocytes with numerous smudge cells.
Peripheral blood flow cytometry: clonal B-cell population co-expressing CD5 and CD23 with dim CD20, kappa light chain restricted.

Impression: chronic lymphocytic leukemia, Rai stage III by anemia, with B symptoms and splenomegaly - meets criteria for treatment.

Plan: acalabrutinib 100 mg twice daily, to start once the specialty pharmacy completes authorization. Counseled on bruising, bleeding, headache, and infection risk; avoid NSAIDs. CBC every 2 weeks for the first month, then monthly. Return in 6 months, sooner as needed.

Thank you for the prompt referral.

ONCOLOGY FOLLOW-UP
Date of visit: 11/02/2023

Diagnoses: CLL, Rai III at diagnosis, on acalabrutinib since 05/2023. Type 2 diabetes. Diabetic foot ulcer right foot. RBD. Thoracic spinal stenosis.

Interval: six months since diagnosis. Today he reports a constant, dull low back ache, not relieved by rest and worse at night, without trauma. He has lost 10 lb over the last two months and has occasional night sweats again.

Medications: acalabrutinib 100 mg BID, metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg daily, melatonin. NKDA.

Exam: tender over the lumbar spinous processes, no step-off or deformity. Straight leg raise negative bilaterally. Strength, sensation and reflexes in the legs unremarkable.

Labs today: hemoglobin 12.5 g/dL (improved from 9.2), ESR 70 mm/hr, calcium 10.2 mg/dL, alkaline phosphatase 120 U/L.

Assessment: new inflammatory-pattern back pain with recurrent weight loss and a high ESR. CLL itself is responding, so we need to exclude a second process in the bone.

Plan: whole-body bone scan and CT chest/abdomen/pelvis with contrast, PSA. Continue acalabrutinib. Will call with results.

CC: primary care

reports.text: CT CHEST WITH IV CONTRAST. Indication: CLL, back pain, weight loss. Mildly enlarged bilateral axillary lymph nodes, largest 1.4 cm short axis. Lungs clear without nodules or consolidation. No pleural or pericardial effusion. Heart normal in size. Sclerotic lesions in several thoracic vertebral bodies and in multiple ribs bilaterally.
reports.conclusion: Sclerotic osseous lesions in thoracic vertebrae and ribs, suspicious for metastases. Mild axillary adenopathy in keeping with known CLL.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: CT ABDOMEN AND PELVIS WITH IV CONTRAST. Spleen mildly enlarged, 14.2 cm. Liver normal without focal lesion. Adrenal glands normal. Kidneys enhance symmetrically without hydronephrosis. No abdominal or pelvic lymphadenopathy by size criteria. Bladder unremarkable. Multiple sclerotic lesions in lumbar vertebral bodies and both iliac bones; no pathologic fracture.
reports.conclusion: Sclerotic lesions of the lumbar spine and pelvis, suspicious for osteoblastic metastases. Mild splenomegaly consistent with known CLL. No visceral metastasis.

ONCOLOGY
Date of letter: 12/08/2023

Dear colleague,

Further to our visit of 11/02, Mr. Kerrigan's workup shows metastatic carcinoma to bone. Bone scan showed widespread osseous uptake in the spine, pelvis and ribs, CT showed corresponding sclerotic lesions without visceral disease, and PSA was 64.8. CT-guided biopsy of the left iliac bone on 11/16/2023 confirmed metastatic adenocarcinoma of prostatic origin (pathology enclosed). He has metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer, alongside his CLL, which continues to respond to acalabrutinib.

Treatment begun:
- Leuprolide 22.5 mg IM every 12 weeks, first dose 11/29/2023.
- Abiraterone 1000 mg daily with prednisone 5 mg daily, started 12/06/2023.
- Acalabrutinib 100 mg twice daily continues.
We will monitor PSA, liver tests, potassium and blood pressure monthly at first. Prednisone may raise his glucose; we would appreciate your help with his diabetes.

Other medications: metformin, lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, melatonin. Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up in 3 months with PSA.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN RECORD
Arrival: 04/25/2025 19:30

CC: shortness of breath, cough.

HPI: 69-year-old man with type 2 diabetes, CLL and metastatic bone disease (prostate primary) presenting with three weeks of progressive exertional dyspnea and a nonproductive cough. Denies chest pain, fever or weight loss.

PMH: as above; RBD; thoracic spinal stenosis; diabetic foot ulcer right foot; retinopathy; hypertension; hyperlipidemia.
Meds: metformin, lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, acalabrutinib, abiraterone, prednisone, leuprolide, melatonin.
Allergies: NKDA.

Triage vitals: BP 145/90, HR 88, RR 20, SpO2 94% on room air.

Exam: speaking full sentences. Breath sounds decreased at the right base. No JVD, no peripheral edema, heart regular without murmur.

Labs: creatinine 1.2, BUN 18, albumin 4.0, total protein 7.2, glucose 160.
Chest radiograph: moderate right pleural effusion, normal heart size, no edema.

Procedure: bedside ultrasound-guided diagnostic thoracentesis, right posterior chest, after consent. 60 mL clear yellow fluid. No complications; post-procedure film without pneumothorax.
Pleural fluid: pH 7.38, glucose 128 mg/dL, protein 4.3 g/dL, LDH 196 U/L, nucleated cells 2,400/uL, neutrophil predominant. Gram stain: no organisms. Culture: no growth (final 04/28). Cytology: negative for malignant cells (final 04/29).

MDM: exudative effusion with neutrophil predominance and reassuring pH and glucose - uncomplicated parapneumonic effusion. No indication for a chest tube. Saturations stable on ambulation.

Disposition: discharged home on levofloxacin 750 mg daily for 7 days. Primary care follow-up within one week; repeat chest x-ray in 4-6 weeks.

reports.text: PA AND LATERAL CHEST. Comparison 04/25/2025. Interval resolution of the right pleural effusion. Costophrenic angles sharp. Lungs clear. Heart size normal. Known sclerotic thoracic spine foci unchanged.
reports.conclusion: Resolved right pleural effusion. No acute cardiopulmonary process.

documents.title: Office Visit

documents.body:
Wife asked for this visit (originally the AWV slot). 

HPI per wife, who is clearly worried: for about six weeks he has been forgetting conversations from the same morning, lost his way driving home from the hardware store, left the stove on twice. Gets confused about the day. More short-tempered than she's ever seen him, and snaps at her, which is not like him. She has also seen sudden quick jerks of his arms, a few times a day, sometimes enough to drop a cup. Francis himself says he's "a little foggy" but minimizes it. No headache, no fall or head injury, no fever. No new medicines. Sleep behavior unchanged.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet; afebrile. Alert, cooperative but slow to answer, repeats questions. MoCA 19/30, losing points on delayed recall, orientation to date, and serial 7s - this from a retired math teacher. Two brief myoclonic jerks of the right arm during the visit. Cranial nerves grossly intact. Strength symmetric. Gait slightly cautious but steady. Neck supple.

A/P: Subacute, rapidly progressive cognitive decline with myoclonus over ~6 weeks. Broad differential; a fast course like this needs neurology quickly.
- CBC, CMP, TSH, B12, RPR today.
- CT head this week.
- Urgent neurology referral (he's known to their practice); I'll call them myself.
- Asked that he stop driving for now; wife will drive. He reluctantly agreed.
- Wife to call with any worsening.

documents.title: Neurology consultation
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
NEUROLOGY
Date of visit: 11/03/2025

Dear colleague,

Thank you for the urgent call about Mr. Kerrigan, whom I have followed for REM sleep behavior disorder since 2021. He has type 2 diabetes, CLL on acalabrutinib, and metastatic prostate cancer to bone on hormonal therapy.

His wife describes a rapid change over roughly three months: worsening memory and confusion, repeated sudden jerks of the limbs, and a change in personality - irritable and withdrawn. He is also sleeping far more than before and struggles to stay awake in the daytime.

Medications: metformin, lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, melatonin 6 mg, acetaminophen as needed, acalabrutinib, abiraterone, prednisone, leuprolide. NKDA.

Examination: disoriented to time and place. Frequent generalized myoclonic jerks. No focal weakness. Not able to complete formal cognitive testing today.

Investigations: routine blood tests (CBC, metabolic panel) are normal; your September TSH, B12 and RPR noted. Lumbar puncture today: CSF WBC 3/mm3, protein 45 mg/dL, glucose 60 mg/dL; 14-3-3 protein positive. EEG: generalized periodic sharp wave complexes.

Impression: rapidly progressive dementia with myoclonus, periodic sharp wave complexes and a positive 14-3-3. This is most consistent with probable sporadic Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease. I have discussed the diagnosis and its expected course frankly with his wife.

Plan:
1. MRI brain with diffusion imaging, scheduled 11/20.
2. CSF RT-QuIC sent to the national prion surveillance laboratory.
3. Levetiracetam 500 mg twice daily for the myoclonus.
4. Standard precautions for any further procedures; the case has been reported to the state health department as required.
5. I recommend early palliative care involvement and would welcome your help with goals-of-care conversations.

I will call his wife with results.

documents.title: Call with neurology
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Spoke with his neurologist. Agrees with letter: probable sporadic CJD, RT-QuIC and MRI pending, expect a course of months. Levetiracetam started for jerks. They'd like us to lead goals-of-care and home support. Already have him booked Friday with wife.

Extended visit with Francis and his wife.

Interval: neurology 11/3 - probable sporadic CJD (14-3-3 positive, periodic sharp waves on EEG); MRI 11/20 and RT-QuIC pending. Started levetiracetam 500 BID; wife thinks the jerks are a little less violent. He sleeps much of the day. Needs help with dressing and showering now. Eating less; weight down. Sleep episodes at night quieter.

Exam: vitals per chart, weight down. Seated in wheelchair the wife brought from a neighbor. Disoriented to date, place and purpose; follows one-step commands inconsistently. Intermittent generalized myoclonic jerks. Lungs clear. Skin intact, sacrum and heels checked, no pressure areas.

Advance care planning (35 min, wife as health care proxy, Francis present and participating as able): reviewed what neurology told them and what to expect. Wife states that Francis always said he would not want to be kept alive by machines. Goals are comfort and staying at home. DNR/DNI agreed; MOLST completed and signed, copy to wife for the refrigerator.

Meds: no changes today; will revisit with palliative care and oncology which cancer and diabetes medicines still help him.

Plan:
1. Probable sporadic CJD - palliative care referral (home-based); home safety (hospital bed and shower chair through palliative/home health).
2. Myoclonus - levetiracetam per neurology.
3. CLL, metastatic prostate cancer - oncology following; wife will tell them about today.
4. DM2 - relaxed targets; avoid lows. Stop finger sticks except if he seems unwell.
5. Caregiver: wife is tired and carrying a lot. Offered social work line; given our direct number.

Wife will message any time.

reports.text: MRI BRAIN WITHOUT CONTRAST. Indication: rapidly progressive dementia, myoclonus. Diffusion-weighted images show restricted diffusion along the cortical ribbon of both cerebral hemispheres and in both caudate heads and putamina, with corresponding low ADC signal. FLAIR shows subtle matching signal. No hemorrhage, mass or hydrocephalus. Mild age-related volume loss.
reports.conclusion: Bilateral cortical ribbon and caudate-putamen diffusion restriction, consistent with prion disease in the appropriate clinical setting.

CSF RT-QuIC returned positive. The MRI of 11/20 shows cortical ribboning and bilateral caudate and putamen diffusion restriction. Together with the clinical picture, positive 14-3-3 and EEG, this fulfils criteria for probable sporadic Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease. I have reviewed the results with his wife by phone. He continues levetiracetam 500 mg twice daily. Palliative care is aware. I am available for any questions and will see him as his family wishes.

HOME-BASED PALLIATIVE CARE CONSULTATION
Visit: 01/06/2026, patient's home

Reason: probable sporadic CJD; also CLL and metastatic prostate cancer.

Since November, Mr. Kerrigan has declined steadily. He can no longer walk without someone holding him and speaks only a few words. His wife provides nearly all care. Myoclonus is present but less disruptive on levetiracetam.

Goals: comfort, home; DNR/DNI with MOLST in place (completed with PCP 11/14).

Recommendations: continue levetiracetam; hospital bed and home health aide arranged; discussed hospice eligibility with his wife, who would like a few weeks to think and to talk with their family. We will see him again in 3 weeks.

Medications reviewed with wife against the bottles; NKDA.

documents.title: RE: Levetiracetam refill
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sent a 90-day supply of levetiracetam 500 mg twice daily to your pharmacy. Thinking of you both. Please reach out if anything changes or if you want to talk through the hospice decision.

documents.title: Hospice admission notice
documents.author: hospice
documents.body:
HOSPICE ADMISSION NOTIFICATION
Admission date: 03/04/2026, routine home care
Terminal diagnosis: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease, probable sporadic. Related: CLL; metastatic prostate adenocarcinoma.

Status at admission: bedbound, minimally verbal, total care by his wife with hospice aides. Hospital bed in place. Code status DNR, MOLST on file.

Medication reconciliation with wife, hospice medical director, and oncology: abiraterone and acalabrutinib discontinued with oncology's agreement; no further leuprolide; prednisone continued for now; metformin discontinued. Continuing levetiracetam 500 mg twice daily, lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide. Comfort medications per hospice protocol.

Please confirm whether you will serve as attending physician of record.

documents.title: Hospice attending confirmation
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hospice RN called. Confirmed I will remain attending of record; signed certification form returned by fax. Wife doing okay with aide support.

documents.title: Hospice interdisciplinary update
documents.author: hospice
documents.body: Hospice IDT summary for attending, period ending 05/08/2026. Patient remains bedbound and minimally verbal, comfortable on current regimen. Skin intact with turning schedule. Wife coping with support from hospice social work and chaplain. Recertified for the next benefit period. No medication changes.

documents.title: Video visit
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, it's Francis's wife again. Hospice is wonderful but I'd like to check in with you about how things are going, and I have some paperwork questions. Could we do one of the video visits in September? Mornings are best.

documents.title: RE: Video visit
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Of course. You're booked for a video visit on Thursday, September 10 at 10:00. The link will come by email the day before.
